MIWI end-to-end flow

The current automation journey and the proposed handling for requests flagged for fraud review, designed to reduce agent handling while keeping decisions consistent, explainable, and reviewable.

01 · Current state

Current flow

The existing journey automates most MIWI requests, with defined cutovers for fraud, policy checks, and system errors.

  1. The customer reports a missing or wrong item.

  2. The system checks the 24-hour reporting window. Requests reported after 24 hours are rejected with the reporting-window reason.

  3. The system checks whether the customer qualifies as a high-value user. Eligible customers bypass standard fraud checks and move directly to image validation.

  4. For all other customers, the system retrieves the TIS fraud assessment.

    • Customers not flagged for fraud proceed to image validation.
    • Fraud-flagged customers are sent to an agent for manual review.

    TIS flags about 8.07% of all tickets for manual review. Agents receive only the fraud outcome, without the signals behind it. They then repeat checks such as Watchtower signals, refund behaviour and frequency, and multiple-account indicators.

  5. Image validation checks whether the submitted image is authentic and relevant to the claim. Invalid images are rejected, but customers may reopen the case with a valid image.

  6. For valid requests, the system determines the eligible refund amount. System errors at this step affect approximately 2.15% of all cases and require manual agent follow-up.

  7. The system applies final checks before completing the refund:

    • Merchant eligibility: 2.7% of all cases are sent for manual check. This includes SG: MCD, PH: Uncle John, and VN: FP Pharmacy.
    • Country refund threshold: 2% of all cases are sent for manual check.
    • Thailand 60/40 discount orders: excluded from automation, with 2.5% of all cases sent for manual check.

  8. After the applicable checks pass, the system pays the refund to the original payment method, GPC, or, where needed, vouchers.

03 · TIS evolution

From a broad flag to an explainable decision

As-is

TIS fraud model

TIS currently flags a case when any of the following conditions is met:

  • The machine-learning fraud score exceeds the defined threshold.
  • The requested refund amount exceeds the refund threshold.
  • The customer exceeds the allowed number of refunds per day.
The model score is not currently explanatory. It indicates potential risk but does not show the specific behaviours or signals behind the result.

Country refund thresholds are also applied in both TIS and Tolong (GSTF), creating overlapping controls.

To-be

Proposed TIS checks

As a short-term solution, use the machine-learning fraud score to trigger additional fraud checks within TIS.

  • If the score does not exceed the threshold, continue with the standard MIWI flow.
  • If the score exceeds the threshold, replace initial agent routing with deterministic fraud checks.
  • Record each check, its inputs, and its outcome on the ticket.
  • Reject the case when one or more checks fail.
  • If no checks fail, continue to image validation.
  • Keep country refund thresholds in Tolong as separate cost and refund-policy controls.

This uses the model score as the initial fraud-risk signal and adds explainable checks on top.

04 · Triggered checks

Checks for customers flagged by the model

Each check runs within TIS only after the model score exceeds the fraud threshold.

90d

Refund-value ratio

Review the last 90 days. Compare total RA value with total completed-order value.

Reject when ratio > 15%
90d

Refund-count ratio

Review the last 90 days. Compare total RA count with total completed orders.

Reject when ratio ≥ 25%
03

Consecutive refunds

Review the last 90 days and identify repeated refund behaviour.

Reject the 3rd consecutive request
LA

Linked accounts

Use the current detection result.

Reject when multiple accounts are detected and at least one is fraud-flagged
PX

PAX-DAX-MEX collusion

Use the current detection result.

Reject when collusion is detected
05 · Proposed state

Proposed decision flow

1
Check for the high-value bypass. If eligible, continue to image validation.
2
Retrieve the TIS fraud outcome for all other customers.
3
If not fraud-flagged, continue to image validation.
4
If fraud-flagged, run every deterministic risk check and store the evidence.
5
Reject if any rule fails. The ticket must show every applicable rejection reason.
6
If no rule fails, continue to image validation, subject to the final policy for fraud-flagged customers.
7
For a valid image, calculate the refund, apply merchant, item, country, and system controls, then pay through the original method, GPC, or vouchers.
06 · Explainability

Audit trail and reopened cases

Agent-ready audit trail

  • TIS fraud status. For every risk rule, show input values, threshold, lookback window, and pass or fail result.
  • High-value bypass status.
  • Image authenticity and relevance result, including the reason for an invalid image.
  • Refund calculation, payment method, and final-control outcomes.

Handling reopened cases

Agents should not repeat checks the automation has already completed. The SOP should distinguish between rejection types:

  • PAX-DAX-MEX collusion or linked fraud account: do not reconsider the refund; keep the rejection in place.
  • Refund ratios or consecutive refunds: review the claim and supporting evidence closely, then reject when proof is insufficient and accept if proof is satisfactory.
